binders: Real space-time variables x and t; the inherited framework is q: R × R → R^m, specialized to q = (p,u) in acoustics. [Printed page 1, (1.1) and following paragraph; printed page 2, (1.6).]

Real-valued fields p(x,t) and u(x,t), representing pressure perturbation and particle velocity. The passage applies generically to fields satisfying the acoustic system, without a separately written universal quantifier. [Printed page 2, (1.5) and explanatory paragraph.]
Constant material parameters K and rho, with c defined by sqrt(K/rho), rather than chosen independently. [Printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5) and definition following (1.6).]
hypotheses: The fields satisfy p_t(x,t) + K u_x(x,t) = 0 and u_t(x,t) + (1/rho) p_x(x,t) = 0 on the domain under consideration. [Printed page 2, (1.5).]
K and rho are constants describing the medium. [Printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5): material described by constants K and rho.]

The connection to the right-moving one-way equation inherits the positive-speed context c > 0. The selected passage does not separately list inequalities on K and rho. [Printed page 2, introduction to (1.4), and passage connecting (1.6) to (1.4).]
conclusions: For w^1(x,t) = p(x,t) + rho c u(x,t), with c = sqrt(K/rho), the field satisfies the actual PDE w^1_t(x,t) + c w^1_x(x,t) = 0. [Printed page 2, definition of w^1 and immediately following displayed equation.]

The coefficient c is identified as the speed of sound, and the resulting equation is the right-moving one-way wave equation introduced in (1.4). [Printed page 2, introduction to (1.4) and sentence following the equation for w^1.]
definitions_and_conventions: Subscripts t and x mean partial differentiation with respect to time and space, respectively. [Printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1).]
p is more precisely a perturbation from a constant background pressure; u is particle velocity. [Printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5).]
K is the bulk modulus of compressibility and rho is density. [Printed page 2, paragraph following (1.5).]
c = sqrt(K/rho) and w^1 = p + rho c u. The superscript 1 labels the mode, as confirmed by the later complementary field w^2. [Printed page 2, definitions of w^1 and w^2.]
The acoustic state has two components q = (p,u), and A has rows (0,K) and (1/rho,0). [Printed page 2, (1.6).]
implicit_context: The chapter considers time-dependent equations in one spatial dimension; its simplest linear framework has constant coefficients. [Printed page 1, introduction to (1.1) and following paragraph.]

Sufficient partial differentiability to interpret the displayed PDEs classically is implicit in the derivative notation and the assertion that the combination satisfies an equation; no named regularity class is supplied. [Printed page 1, derivative convention; printed page 2, (1.5) and equation for w^1.]

The source says the full acoustic equations are derived in Chapter 2. On the supplied page, they are presented directly as the system from which the mode claim follows. [Printed page 2, sentence introducing (1.5).]

The neighboring complementary claim is that w^2 = p - rho c u satisfies w^2_t - c w^2_x = 0 and propagates left with speed -c. It is a separate assertion in the enclosing discussion, outside the locator's selected right-mode equation. [Printed page 2, passage beginning 'On the other hand' and final paragraph.]

details: The conclusion concerns a function constructed from solutions of coupled PDEs and its partial derivatives, not merely an identity among unrelated scalar symbols. [Printed page 1, derivative convention; printed page 2, (1.5) and definition and equation of w^1.]

The coefficients rho and c in the mode combination are independent of x and t because the material parameters are constant and c is defined from them. [Printed page 2, material-constant paragraph and c = sqrt(K/rho).]

Using c^2 = K/rho in an algebraic derivation requires the real square root to have its intended nonnegative radicand; this requirement is an analyst inference from the displayed definition, not a separately stated hypothesis on the page. [Printed page 2, c = sqrt(K/rho).]
The plus sign in p + rho c u corresponds to the plus sign in w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0 and positive rightward speed c. [Printed page 2, (1.4) and the two displays defining and governing w^1.]
The minus combination is explicitly associated with the opposite propagation direction. [Printed page 2, displays defining and governing w^2 and final paragraph.]

The mode assertion specifies no initial data, boundary data, normalization of p or u, existence theorem, or uniqueness theorem. Its stated inputs are the acoustic system and the defined combination. [Printed page 2, (1.5) through the equation for w^1.]

contract_plain_english: For pressure perturbation p and particle velocity u satisfying the constant-coefficient acoustic system p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0, define c = sqrt(K/rho) and w^1 = p + rho c u. The source asserts that this field satisfies w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0, with actual partial derivatives, and identifies c as the sound speed in the positive rightward-propagation context. [Printed page 1, derivative convention following (1.1); printed page 2, (1.4)–(1.6) and the subsequent w^1 passage.] Differentiability and material-parameter admissibility are implicit rather than separately enumerated hypotheses. [Printed page 2, (1.5) and c = sqrt(K/rho).]
